name: Pilgrimage and heritage
short: The sacred sites of the island, visited with time, respect and a guide who knows them.
summary: The island's sacred sites, from the Temple of the Tooth to the places of the Ramayana, visited with time, care and a guide who knows them.

image.alt: Gilded Buddhas in the Dambulla cave temples

suits.heading: Sacred places, visited properly.
suits.body: We plan the visits around ceremony times and festival days, with guides who know the customs and the stories.

services.heading: What we look after.
services.body: The visits, and the care around them.

items.title: Guides who know the sites
items.body: Guides who speak your language and can explain the history and the practice.

items.title: Timed to ceremony
items.body: Visits planned around pujas and festival days, such as the Esala Perahera in Kandy.

items.title: Group transport
items.body: Coaches and vans sized to the group, with assistance for older travellers.

items.title: Food and stays
items.body: Vegetarian and sattvic menus, and stays close to the sites.

items.title: Offerings and dress
items.body: Guidance on what to wear and bring, and flowers or offerings arranged where they are needed.

shapes.heading: Shapes we often plan.
shapes.lede: Starting points, each planned around your group's practice.

items.title: The Cultural Triangle
items.body: Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa, Dambulla and Kandy, with time at each and no rushing.

items.title: The Ramayana trail
items.body: The sites linked to the Ramayana, from the hill country to the south.

items.title: Kandy at festival time
items.body: The Temple of the Tooth and the Esala Perahera, with seats arranged ahead.

questions.q: Can you arrange vegetarian food throughout?
questions.a: Yes. We agree vegetarian, Jain or sattvic menus with every hotel and restaurant on the route.
It is usually in July or August, set by the lunar calendar. Ask us and we will confirm the dates for your year.
